passages.scripture: In my first book, O Theophilus, I wrote about all that Jesus began to do and to teach, until the day He was taken up to heaven, after giving instructions through the Holy Spirit to the apostles He had chosen.

lines.text: Luke wrote his first book to a man named Theophilus.
That book told about everything Jesus began to do.
That book also told everything Jesus began to teach.
That book told about Jesus, until the day He was taken up to heaven.
Before Jesus was taken up to heaven, He gave instructions to His apostles, the men He sent out.
Jesus gave these instructions through the Holy Spirit.
Jesus had chosen these apostles Himself.

passages.scripture: After His suffering, He presented Himself to them with many convincing proofs that He was alive. He appeared to them over a span of forty days and spoke about the kingdom of God.

lines.text: After Jesus suffered and died, Jesus showed Himself alive to the apostles.
Jesus gave them many convincing proofs that He was alive.
Jesus appeared to the apostles over forty days.
And Jesus spoke to them about the kingdom of God — the kingdom of God is where God reigns as King.

passages.scripture: And while they were gathered together, He commanded them: “Do not leave Jerusalem, but wait for the gift the Father promised, which you have heard Me discuss.

lines.text: Jesus was gathered together with the apostles.
Jesus commanded them:
Jesus said, “Do not leave Jerusalem” — Jerusalem was the chief city of the Jews, where the temple of God stood.
Jesus said, “Instead, wait for the gift the Father promised” — the gift is the Holy Spirit.
Jesus said, “You have heard Me talk about this promise.”
Earlier Jesus promised the apostles that He would send them the gift of the Holy Spirit from the Father.

passages.scripture: For John baptized with water, but in a few days you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.”

lines.text: Jesus told His apostles, “John the Baptist baptized people with water.”
Jesus said to them, “But you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.”
Jesus said this would happen in a few days.
John the Baptist himself had said that Jesus would baptize people with the Holy Spirit.

passages.scripture: So when they came together, they asked Him, “Lord, will You at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?”

lines.text: So the apostles came together with Jesus.
The apostles asked Jesus a question.
The apostles said, “Lord, will You at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?” — would Israel now be freed from Rome and be its own kingdom again?

passages.scripture: Jesus replied, “It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has fixed by His own authority.

lines.text: Jesus replied to the apostles' question about Israel being its own kingdom.
Jesus said to the apostles, “It is not for you to know times or seasons.” — it was not for the apostles to know when Israel would become its own kingdom.
Jesus said the Father has fixed these times and seasons — to fix a time is to decide when it will happen.
And Jesus said the Father fixed these times and seasons by His own authority — His authority is the power to decide.

passages.scripture: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you, and you will be My witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.”

lines.text: Jesus told His apostles, “But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you” — instead of promising power to the kingdom of Israel now, Jesus promised the apostles power in the kingdom of God.
Jesus said, “But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you” — the power Jesus promised was not from the apostles, but from the Holy Spirit.
Jesus said, “And you will be My witnesses” — a witness tells others what they have seen for themselves.
Jesus said, “And you will be My witnesses” — the apostles had seen Jesus alive after He rose, so they could testify that Jesus rose to life.
Jesus said, “You will be My witnesses in Jerusalem” — Jerusalem is where the apostles already were, so they began testifying about Jesus where they were.
Jesus said, “You will be My witnesses in all Judea and Samaria” — Judea and Samaria were neighboring regions, with Jerusalem located in Judea.
Jesus said, “You will be My witnesses in all Judea and Samaria” — the Jews avoided the Samaritans, yet Jesus sends His witnesses to them too.
Jesus said, “And you will be My witnesses to the ends of the earth” — the ends of the earth means everywhere in the world, however far away.

passages.scripture: After He had said this, they watched as He was taken up, and a cloud hid Him from their sight.

lines.text: Jesus finished telling His apostles they would be His witnesses.
The apostles watched as Jesus was taken up into heaven.
Jesus was taken up by the power of God.
Then a cloud hid Jesus from the apostles.
The apostles could no longer see Jesus.

passages.scripture: They were looking intently into the sky as He was going, when suddenly two men dressed in white stood beside them.

lines.text: The apostles kept looking intently into the sky.
Jesus was going up, and the apostles were still watching.
Suddenly two men stood beside the apostles.
The two men were dressed in white.

passages.scripture: “Men of Galilee,” they said, “why do you stand here looking into the sky? This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen Him go into heaven.”

lines.text: The two men said to the apostles, “Men of Galilee” — Galilee is in northern Israel, where these apostles came from.
The two men asked, “Why do you stand here looking into the sky?”
The two men said, “This same Jesus has been taken from you into heaven.”
The two men said, “This same Jesus will come back.”

The two men said, “Jesus will come back in the same way you have seen Him go into heaven” — the apostles watched a cloud hide Jesus as He ascended into heaven, and in the same way Jesus will return in the sky and on the clouds.

passages.scripture: Then they returned to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives, which is near the city, a Sabbath day’s journey away.

lines.text: Then the apostles returned to Jerusalem.
The apostles came back from the Mount of Olives — a long hill named for the olive trees that grew on it.
The Mount of Olives is near the city of Jerusalem.
The Mount of Olives is a Sabbath day’s journey away from Jerusalem — about one kilometer.
A Sabbath day’s journey is how far people were allowed to walk on the Sabbath — the weekly day of rest.

passages.scripture: When they arrived, they went to the upper room where they were staying: Peter and John, James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James.

lines.text: When the apostles arrived in Jerusalem, they went to the upper room — a room upstairs in a house.
The apostles were staying in the upper room.
Peter and John were there, and so were James and Andrew.
And Philip and Thomas were there, as well as Bartholomew and Matthew.
James son of Alphaeus was there — a different James from James the brother of John.
And Simon the Zealot was there — “Zealot” means someone eager, devoted and full of zeal.
And Judas son of James was there — not Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus.

passages.scripture: With one accord they all continued in prayer, along with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with His brothers.

lines.text: The apostles all devoted themselves to prayer — they kept praying constantly.
The apostles prayed with one accord — united, with one mind and one purpose.
Some women prayed with the apostles.
Mary, the mother of Jesus, prayed with the apostles.
The brothers of Jesus also prayed with the apostles.
Earlier, the brothers of Jesus had not believed in Him — now they were praying with His apostles.

passages.scripture: In those days Peter stood up among the brothers (a gathering of about a hundred and twenty) and said, “Brothers, the Scripture had to be fulfilled which the Holy Spirit foretold through the mouth of David concerning Judas, who became a guide for those who arrested Jesus.

lines.text: In those days, Peter stood up among the brothers.
Here “brothers” means fellow believers in Jesus — not brothers by birth.
About one hundred and twenty believers were gathered together.
Peter said, “Brothers, the Scripture had to be fulfilled.”
What God says in Scripture must come true.
Peter said, “The Holy Spirit foretold this Scripture through the mouth of David.”
David spoke the words, and the Holy Spirit was speaking through David.
To foretell is to say something before it happens.
Peter said, “This Scripture was about Judas Iscariot, who became a guide for those who arrested Jesus.”
Judas Iscariot led the men who came to arrest Jesus to where Jesus was.

passages.scripture: He was one of our number and shared in this ministry.”

lines.text: Judas Iscariot was counted as one of the twelve apostles — Jesus had chosen Judas Iscariot to be one of the twelve.
Peter said, “Judas Iscariot was one of our number.”
Judas Iscariot was given a share in this ministry.
This ministry was the work of serving as an apostle of Jesus.

passages.scripture: (Now with the reward for his wickedness Judas bought a field; there he fell headlong and burst open in the middle, and all his intestines spilled out.

lines.text: Judas Iscariot bought a field with the reward for his wickedness.
The reward for the wickedness of Judas Iscariot was the money Judas Iscariot was paid for betraying Jesus.
Judas Iscariot fell headlong — head first.
The body of Judas Iscariot burst open in the middle.
All the intestines of Judas Iscariot spilled out.
